newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oct industrial output fell 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oct industrial output fell 0.5 pct.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board report of U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization, seasonally adjusted.

The drop in October industrial output was the first monthly decline since March, when it also fell 0.5 percent. October's capacity use rate of 82.7 percent was the lowest since last March when it was 82.6 percent.
Wall Street economists expected October industrial production to be unchanged from September and estimated that October capacity use would be at a rate of 83.0 percent.

The Fed said sharp drops in production of motor vehicles and parts accounted for the decrease in the overall index last month. Motor vehicle assemblies fell because of strikes at General Motors plants in Canada and the United States.
Manufacturing output dropped 0.5 percent in October, its first drop since a 0.9 percent decline in March.
Motor vehicle assemblies fell in October to a rate of 5.5 million a year for automobiles from 6.5 million in September. For light trucks the assembly rate was unchanged at 5.4 million.
Excluding motor vehicles and parts, October industrial output declined only 0.1 percent after rising 0.4 percent in September.
